config.title: Request & Response

intro.title: Request & Response
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Express server that handles incoming HTTP requests and sends back custom responses. You will learn the core concepts of the request and response objects, which are fundamental to web development. The main technologies involved are the Express framework and JavaScript, using methods like `req.params` to access URL data and `res.send()` to return content. By the end, you'll understand how to read client input and dynamically generate server replies.
intro.usecase: Every time you submit a form, click a button, or navigate between pages in a web application, you're triggering requests and responses. In Express, this pattern powers user interactions like submitting contact forms, adding items to shopping carts, or filtering search results on e-commerce sites. As a developer, you'll use request objects to access user input (like form data or URL parameters) and response objects to send back appropriate content—whether it's rendering a dashboard with updated analytics or returning JSON data for a mobile app. Understanding this request-response cycle is fundamental to building any interactive web feature that processes user actions and provides dynamic feedback.

objectives: Initialize an Express application to handle HTTP requests.
Configure route handlers to respond to different HTTP methods.
Extract and manipulate data from incoming request objects.
Construct and send response objects with appropriate status codes and content.
Integrate middleware to process requests before reaching route handlers.
Apply query parameters and route parameters to customize responses.
Control response headers and content types for different client needs.

steps.title: Import Express and create a basic Express app
steps.instruction: Import the Express module and create an Express application instance.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import Express and assign it to a variable. Then create an app instance by calling the imported Express function.
steps.seedCode: // Import Express and create an app instance here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an Express app instance ready to configure routes and handle requests.
successCriteria: Express is imported using require() and an app instance is created by calling express().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've both imported Express (using require('express')) and created an app instance (by calling express()).
steps.feedbackWrong: import the Express module and create an application instance. Check the analogous example for reference.

steps.title: Create a basic GET route handler for the root path
steps.instruction: Add a GET route handler for the root path '/' that sends a simple text response 'Hello from Express!'
steps.hint: Use app.get() with the path '/' and a callback function that takes request and response objects. Call res.send() with your text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will respond to GET requests to the root URL with the text 'Hello from Express!'
successCriteria: A GET route handler for '/' is defined using app.get() and sends a text response with res.send()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using app.get() with '/' as the first argument and a callback function that calls res.send() with the text response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route handler isn't quite right. Remember to use app.get('/', ...) with a function that takes req and res parameters, then call res.send('Hello from Express!') inside it.

steps.title: Examine the request object properties
steps.instruction: Inside your existing GET route handler for '/', add a console.log statement to output the request method and URL from the request object.
steps.hint: The request object is available as the first parameter in your route handler callback. Use req.method and req.url to access these properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: When you run the app and make a GET request to the root path, the server console will display the request method and URL.
successCriteria: The route handler includes a console.log statement that outputs both req.method and req.url.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your console.log includes both req.method and req.url properties from the request object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route handler should include a console.log statement that outputs both the request method and URL. Check that you're using req.method and req.url inside your route handler callback.

steps.title: Access query parameters from the request
steps.instruction: Create a new GET route for '/search' that reads query parameters from the request object and responds with them in a JSON format.
steps.hint: Use req.query to access query parameters. Respond with res.json() to send them back as JSON.
steps.expectedOutcome: When you test the '/search' route with query parameters (e.g., /search?q=express&sort=desc), the server should respond with a JSON object containing those parameters.
successCriteria: A GET route for '/search' exists that uses req.query to access query parameters and responds with res.json() containing those parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your route uses req.query to get the parameters and res.json() to send them back.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route doesn't seem to be reading query parameters correctly. Check that you're using req.query and responding with res.json().

steps.title: Access route parameters from the request
steps.instruction: Create a new GET route for '/users/:id' that extracts the 'id' parameter from the request object and sends it back in the response.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with a path containing ':id'. Inside the handler, access req.params.id and send it back using res.send().
steps.expectedOutcome: A new route '/users/:id' is added that responds with the id parameter value from the URL.
successCriteria: The route '/users/:id' is defined with app.get(), accesses req.params.id, and sends it in the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.get() with '/users/:id', accessing req.params.id, and sending it in the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using the correct path syntax with ':id' and accessing the parameter from req.params.

steps.title: Set response status codes
steps.instruction: In the '/users/:id' route handler, set the response status code to 200 before sending the response.
steps.hint: Use the res.status() method to set the HTTP status code, then chain .send() to send the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: The '/users/:id' route will respond with a 200 OK status code and the user ID message.
successCriteria: The route handler uses res.status(200) before sending the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using res.status(200) before sending the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route handler doesn't set the status code correctly. Use res.status(200) before .send().

steps.title: Send JSON responses
steps.instruction: Create a new GET route for '/api/data' that sends a JSON response containing an object with a 'message' property set to 'Hello from JSON!' using res.json().
steps.hint: Use app.get() with the path '/api/data' and a callback that takes req and res parameters. Inside the callback, call res.json() with an object like { message: 'Hello from JSON!' }.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new route '/api/data' that responds with JSON data when accessed via GET request.
successCriteria: The route '/api/data' is defined with app.get() and uses res.json() to send an object with a 'message' property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using res.json() with an object containing a 'message' property, and the route path should be '/api/data'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route for sending JSON isn't set up correctly. Check that you've defined a GET route for '/api/data' and used res.json() with an object.

steps.title: Set response headers
steps.instruction: In the '/api/data' route handler, set a custom 'Content-Type' header to 'application/json' before sending the JSON response.
steps.hint: Use the res.set() or res.setHeader() method to add the header. The header name is 'Content-Type' and the value is 'application/json'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The '/api/data' route will send a JSON response with the correct 'Content-Type' header set to 'application/json'.
successCriteria: The '/api/data' route handler uses res.set() or res.setHeader() to set 'Content-Type' to 'application/json' before calling res.json().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're setting the 'Content-Type' header with value 'application/json' before sending the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header wasn't set correctly. Use res.set('Content-Type', 'application/json') or res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json') in the '/api/data' route handler.

steps.title: Handle POST requests with request body
steps.instruction: Create a POST route handler for '/submit' that reads JSON data from the request body and responds with it.
steps.hint: Use app.post() with '/submit' as the path. The request body will contain JSON data, which you can access via req.body. Send it back as JSON using res.json().
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST route at '/submit' that reads JSON from req.body and sends it back as JSON.
successCriteria: The code includes app.post('/submit', (req, res) => { ... }) that uses req.body and responds with res.json().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.post() with '/submit', accessing req.body, and sending a JSON response.
steps.feedbackWrong: This step requires creating a POST route for '/submit' that reads from req.body and responds with JSON. Check your route method and response.

steps.title: Start the Express server and test all routes
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling app.listen() on port 3000 and add a console.log to confirm it's running.
steps.hint: Use app.listen(port, callback) to start the server. The callback should log a message like 'Server running on port 3000'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start on port 3000 and log a confirmation message when running.
successCriteria: The server is started with app.listen() on port 3000 and includes a console.log callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling app.listen() with port 3000 and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't started correctly. You need to call app.listen(3000, callback) to start the server on port 3000.
